spec_match.rationale: Pins both halves of Appendix A: used values still truncate/repeat (side-by-side identical paint), while computed values flow intact through inherit and through transition interpolation — the two places the change is observable beyond readback.

interactive.rationale: Three real probes: compare button reads A/B computed lists, inherit button measures what a genuine DOM child receives (via a hidden inheriting probe applied verbatim to the visible stage), spread toggle moves the parent's 3rd entry, and the transition button samples the computed list mid-flight.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises the unchanged-paint proof plus live inherit and transition reads; all present.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers the none-counts-as-one-layer side probe in the banner, the inherit truncation pile-up, the matched-paint invariant, and prefers-reduced-motion shortens the transition.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus, Appendix A and the interpolation WPT alongside sibling concepts.

conformance.rationale: The suite's inherit-passes-full-computed-list, none-layer and used-value-rendering-invariant assertions are this page's exact cases; the rendering-invariant assertion passes on both engine generations by design.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless via CDP: A/B computed reads showed truncation with identical paint (screenshots show matching single dots), inherited list measured 1 entry with the child's three dots visibly superimposed, spread toggle correctly narrated the child's blindness to the 3rd entry, mid-transition sample returned one interpolating entry (79.99px); console clean; both viewports screenshot-verified.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts probe consistency (truncation and none-layer agree), paint equivalence, and that inherit/transition entry counts match the detected tier.

design_system.rationale: All chrome from design-system variables; dot gradients use accent variables with no text on them.

accessibility.rationale: Paint stages carry role=img labels describing spread-vs-piled outcomes, buttons are native with 44px targets and the spread toggle exposes aria-pressed, single polite readout region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Panes stack via auto-fit grid at 360×740 DPR3 with no horizontal overflow; both classes screenshot-verified.

openQuestions.title: Verify the spread-out child and two-entry transition on Chrome 158+/Canary
openQuestions.detail: On 158 the inherit button must report 3 entries with the child's dots spread (rose dot following the spread toggle), and the mid-transition sample must carry two interpolating entries. Only the truncated branches could execute on Chromium 141.

openQuestions.title: Deepen the interpolation angle once 158 is testable
openQuestions.detail: List interpolation between different-length lists (repeat-to-LCM pairing) only becomes observable when computed lists are preserved; once a 158 runtime is available, consider extending the transition section (or an additive concept) to animate mismatched-length lists and read the LCM pairing live. Recorded here because the advanced/composition angle is folded into this page per the index research record.

openQuestions.title: Inspect the accessibility tree with chrome-devtools-mcp
openQuestions.detail: role=img labels and the toggle's pressed state were not inspected in the accessibility tree; chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable (project rule 7b).

guidanceConsulted.query: side-by-side comparison panes that stack on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Auto-fit minmax grids for comparison panes; never fixed two-column layouts on narrow screens.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: No page overflow at 360×740; mobile screenshots read.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Visual-only state needs text equivalents tied to the output.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each stage's aria-label describes both possible outcomes (spread vs piled), and every button press writes the verdict into the polite readout.
The transition stage drops to 0.01s duration under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce; the sample button still reports honestly.

summary: Edge page verified on Chromium 141 headless: identical paint under truncation proven side by side, real inheritance measured at 1 entry with the pile-up visible, spread toggle and mid-transition sampling all narrated honestly; console clean; both viewports pass. The preserved-tier outcomes (3-entry inherit, 2-entry interpolation) await Chrome 158.
